method: Same selection system as live play: random subjects and formats, then random unseen questions. Recent subjects are avoided to keep the mix varied; first 100.

questions.prompt: Name a named type of bread.
questions.scope: Named breads, rolls and flatbreads count; filling-only variations do not create a new bread.

questions.prompt: Name something that produces visible light.
questions.scope: Natural sources and human-made devices count; a reflector alone does not.

questions.prompt: Name a video game where the player can go fishing.
questions.scope: A player-controlled fishing activity counts, including optional minigames.

questions.prompt: Name a movie involving time travel or a time loop.
questions.scope: Films in which characters travel through time or experience a repeating time loop count, including animated movies and shorts. Ordinary flashbacks, dreams about the past and a futuristic setting alone do not count.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with metal music.
Name a plant that has thorns, spines or prickles.
questions.scope: The sharp growth can be on any ordinary part of the plant; edible plants count too.

questions.prompt: Name a water sport or recreational activity on or in water.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a landlocked country.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name an object that commonly has a hinge.
questions.scope: A common hinged version of the object must exist. Sliding or roll-up versions do not prevent a genuinely hinged object from counting.

questions.prompt: Name a Legendary or Mythical Pokémon.
questions.scope: Species classified as Legendary or Mythical in the pinned PokéAPI data count. Forms share their species' answer identity. Pseudo-Legendary is a fan label and does not make a species Legendary.

questions.prompt: Name a type of sausage, including regional and cured varieties.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a percussion instrument.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a material or substance used to make things.
Name a kind of parrot.
questions.scope: Parrot species and established named groups count, including recently extinct species in the source taxonomy. Common and scientific names count. Pet colour mutations share their species identity; a bird is not a parrot just because its name contains that word.

questions.prompt: Name a spoken, signed or constructed language.
Name an everyday object with wheels.
questions.scope: Ordinary objects and vehicles count; named types count without needing a brand.

questions.prompt: Name someone who has played in the WNBA.
Name an animation movie.
Name a music act known as a duo.
questions.scope: Current and historical musical duos count. Ordinary backing musicians do not change a two-person act into a larger group. Two solo artists who collaborated once are not automatically a named duo.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish or preparation in which eggs are a main ingredient.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of animal that can pollinate flowers.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a city that has hosted the modern Olympics.
questions.scope: Summer and Winter hosts count; ancient host cities alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a type of room or specialized indoor space.
Name a flower or flowering block found in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Flower items and blocks count, including tall flowers and Nether-compatible flowers. Named crops and saplings do not become flowers merely because they are plants. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a brand that makes athletic shoes.
questions.scope: Real sports-footwear brands count, including specialist running and court-shoe brands.

questions.prompt: Name a musical artist or band with a number in their name.
questions.scope: Numbers written as digits, words or Roman numerals count.

questions.prompt: Name a dumpling or established regional dumpling variety.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of marsupial. Named groups and species, living or extinct, count; a common or scientific name is accepted.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a tool, instrument or piece of glassware used in a science laboratory.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a crime TV or streaming show.
Name a tool or piece of equipment used for gardening.
questions.scope: Tools, devices and durable equipment used to plant, water, prune, move soil or maintain gardens count. Plant names are not tools.

questions.prompt: Name a river, lake, sea, ocean, gulf, bay or strait.
Name a musician known professionally by one name.
questions.scope: An established one-word stage name counts even when their legal name has several words.

questions.prompt: Name a champion in League of Legends.
questions.scope: Base-game and recorded expansion names count. Versions of the same named object count once.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish commonly made with chicken.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name one of the 88 official constellations.
questions.scope: Official IAU constellation names count. Recognized common names such as Capricorn and the Great Bear are accepted. Asterisms such as the Big Dipper are only parts of constellations.

questions.prompt: Name a horror movie.
Name a piece of camping equipment.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a government-issued currency, monetary unit or named historical coin.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name an insect.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Horror”.
Name a combat sport or established martial art.
questions.scope: Named competitive fighting disciplines and established martial arts count, including forms practiced without full-contact competition. Fictional styles do not count.

questions.prompt: Name something people put inside a sandwich.
questions.scope: Established sandwich fillings count, including spreads and condiments.

questions.prompt: Name an animated TV series.
questions.scope: Shows for any audience count, including cartoons, anime and streaming series.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with k-pop music.
Name a type of rock.
questions.scope: Recognized geological rock names, rock families and established natural stone varieties count. Common and scientific rock names are accepted. Individual minerals, chemical elements, whole mountains and manufactured building products are not rock types.

questions.prompt: Name a type of shop.
Name a landmark people can visit.
questions.scope: Named natural or human-made visitor landmarks count, including ruins.

questions.prompt: Name an emote from Fortnite.
questions.scope: Any recorded season or collaboration counts. These are cosmetic names, not Battle Royale weapon names.

questions.prompt: Name a wild animal that spends time both in water and on land.
questions.scope: The animal must normally use both habitats, not merely survive a brief swim.

questions.prompt: Name a science fiction movie.
Name a musical genre or subgenre.
Name a vegetable or edible plant part commonly cooked as a vegetable.
Name a scientist, mathematician, inventor or science communicator.
Name an item used in a bathroom.
questions.scope: Established bathroom, bathing, grooming and hygiene items count.

questions.prompt: Name a driver who has competed in Formula One.
questions.scope: Drivers in the complete Jolpica/Ergast Formula One World Championship driver inventory count, including historical entrants and the Indianapolis 500 when it was part of that championship. A real surname can identify a valid driver; invented initials and racing three-letter codes do not count as names.

questions.prompt: Name a volcano or named volcanic complex. Dormant and extinct ones count.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a playable hero in Overwatch.
questions.scope: The full official Overwatch roster in the October 25, 2026 snapshot counts, including heroes introduced while it was called Overwatch 2. Skins and unplayable story characters do not.

questions.prompt: Name a fictional pirate.
questions.scope: Named fictional sea, air and space pirates count, including characters who were pirates earlier in their story. A smuggler, sailor or marine is not automatically a pirate.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of animal that can regrow a lost body part.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a human muscle or muscle group.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a music group with at least three members.
questions.scope: Bands and vocal groups from any era count; a solo artist's unnamed backing band does not.

questions.prompt: Name an item or product used to wash, dry or care for laundry.
questions.scope: Laundry appliances, supplies, stain treatments and clothes-care tools count, as do named product types and established laundry-product brands, including historical ones. A garment itself is not a laundry supply.

questions.prompt: Name a sport or recognized sporting discipline played on snow or ice.
questions.scope: Established ice and snow sports and competitive disciplines count. A sport merely played during the winter on an ordinary indoor court does not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a candy or chocolate brand.
questions.scope: Brands and named candy products count; ordinary flavor names alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a landform, natural feature or kind of landscape.
Name a kind of owl.
questions.scope: Owl species and established named groups count, including recently extinct species in the source taxonomy. Common names and scientific names count. An owlet-nightjar or a nighthawk is not an owl.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Sandbox”.
Name a stringed musical instrument.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a movie that is a sequel to another movie.
questions.scope: Direct sequels count, even if there is no number in the title.

questions.prompt: Name a gesture or bodily signal.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name a chemical element used in everyday products.
questions.scope: There must be a documented consumer, industrial or medical use; exact product names are not required.

questions.prompt: Name a stadium, arena or racetrack used for professional sports.
questions.scope: Named venues anywhere in the world count; past venue names would be aliases.

questions.prompt: Name a dessert, sweet dish, or confection.
Name a kind of animal that has a protective shell, carapace, bony plates or body armour.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with country music.
Name an anime TV or streaming show.
Name a country whose national flag contains a star.
questions.scope: A visible star on the official national flag qualifies; tiny stars inside a coat of arms count too.

questions.prompt: Name a chemical element. Symbols count.
Name a type of sports equipment.
Name an object designed to be inflated.
questions.scope: Common inflatable objects and named inflatable equipment types count, whether filled with air, helium or another gas. Objects merely containing an empty cavity do not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of penguin.
questions.scope: Species in the eBird/Clements penguin order and established common group names count. English or scientific names count. Puffins and auks are different kinds of bird.

questions.prompt: Name a food commonly cooked by frying.
questions.scope: Named foods and dishes count; a one-off experiment is not enough.

questions.prompt: Name something a player can eat in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Vanilla food items count, including foods with negative effects.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with rock music.
Name a real, named bridge.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a body part a typical human has more than one of.
questions.scope: Named bones, organs and body parts count; ordinary singular names would be accepted.

questions.prompt: Name something students bring to school.
questions.scope: Physical items brought for an ordinary school day count; people and pets do not.

questions.prompt: Name a dog breed, including historical breeds.
Name a quarterback who started and won a Super Bowl.
questions.scope: The quarterback must have started a winning Super Bowl, through Super Bowl LX in February 2026. Winning a ring as a backup alone does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a block an Enderman can pick up in Minecraft.
questions.scope: The actual block-pickup rule counts, including flowers. Endermen may pick up only certain blocks even if the player can carry other blocks. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a dance style, traditional dance, or named social dance.
Name an amusement park or theme-park resort.
questions.scope: Real parks and resort complexes count worldwide; familiar resort names would be accepted.

questions.prompt: Name a food commonly served on a stick.
questions.scope: Named foods and established skewer dishes count, including sweets.

questions.prompt: Name something people can borrow from a public library.
questions.scope: Items must actually be offered by a public library somewhere; Library of Things collections count.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that changes color.
questions.scope: Rapid camouflage and seasonal changes both count.

questions.prompt: Name a sport or competitive game.
Name a type of creature from mythology, folklore, or fantasy.
Name a musical instrument played by blowing air into it.
questions.scope: Mouth-blown instruments count, including reed, brass and free-reed instruments.

questions.prompt: Name a food named after a place.
questions.scope: The place name must appear in an established food or dish name.
